extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper dispatch reporting air raids, military movements and civilian impact during wartime (Battle of Britain-era reporting), using official statements, eyewitness accounts and on-the-ground detail to inform the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute to official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite government or military authorities (e.g., 'the Air Ministry announced', 'a British communique charged', 'the German High Command said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named official sources for claims about military actions and results; quote or paraphrase communiques and ministries to show provenance of information (examples throughout: 'The Air Ministry announced...', 'A British communique charges that...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eyewitness and observer accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Include first-person or observer reports to convey immediate details (e.g., 'The observer of a bomber which was about to release its own missile read...', 'rescue crews found two babies still alive beneath the mass of rubble').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement official statements with observers' descriptions to provide concrete, human-scale detail and vivid scenes; attribute these accounts clearly to observers or rescue crews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report precise times and locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Give specific times and place names for events and signals (e.g., 'sirens at 3:20 P. M. (10:20 A. M., New York time)', 'all-clear sounded at 4:40 P. M.', locations like 'Calais', 'Dover', 'London').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide time stamps, local and translated zones, and exact place names to situate readers and allow verification or cross-referencing of events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe impact on civilians and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Document damage to homes, hospitals, transport and utilities and human consequences (e.g., 'bombs demolished a big apartment building', 'a large maternity hospital [was] hit', 'workmen still were struggling to restore some of the transportation, water and gas services').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report concrete effects on daily life and essential services to convey the human cost and operational consequences of attacks; include sheltering, evacuations, and relief efforts where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide strategic and contextual analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain broader military significance and likely courses of action (e.g., 'The trend of the conflict will depend in no small degree on how [civilian morale] is concerned', 'barges concentrations ... indicate a full-scale invasion of this island is being prepared').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond immediate facts, interpret what actions and patterns imply for the campaign—use expert statements, official warnings, and reported concentrations/movements to assess intent and likely next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include operational details of attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on targets, tactics and munitions (e.g., 'ports were heavily pounded', 'sticks of heavy bombs straddled barges', 'high explosives poured into the packed vessels').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which military or logistical targets were struck, the manner of attack, and observable effects (fires, explosions, ships burning) to convey the character and effectiveness of operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note environmental and weather factors affecting operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention how weather (fogs, mists, clouds, night conditions) affects bombing and reconnaissance (e.g., discussion of English fogs and instrument-flying, 'bad weather ... failed to balk the raiders').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how meteorological conditions influence the ability of aircraft to locate and strike targets, and how authorities manage or conceal weather information for military advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute uncertainty and withhold unverified figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear when numbers or details are not yet confirmed (e.g., 'Casualty figures have not been announced', 'preliminary reports indicate ... casualties are considerably lighter').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting unverified casualty or damage totals; state provisional status and continue to update as official or corroborated figures become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey human-interest rescue and relief activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Report actions of rescue crews, sheltering, medical aid and refugee movements (e.g., 'rescue crews dug into new heaps of debris to save the living and carry out the dead', 'nearly 500 persons, homeless after earlier raids, were sheltered in the building').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of civilian relief efforts, medical treatment, sheltering and evacuation plans to illustrate response capacity and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid sensory and narrative detail to convey atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ descriptive language that captures sound, sight and mood (e.g., 'the drone of airplane motors', 'roof tops were empty of watchers', 'the rolling thud of bombs').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evocative, concrete imagery and sensory detail to help readers understand the experience of raids while balancing against gratuitous sensationalism; anchor such descriptions with attribution or source where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronicle sequence and repetition of events for pattern recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Show temporal patterns (e.g., 'fourth successive night of the raids', 'three more air-raid alarms were sounded', 'Repeatedly sticks of heavy bombs').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the cadence and repetition of attacks to reveal escalation, lull, or change in tactics; use past sequence to inform present risk assessments.
